title: Tesla unveils new Roadster with flight capabilities; set for production in 2028
full_text:
Nasdaq ends higher in big rebound as bond rally offsets tech softness, hot PPI
Investing.com-- Tesla unveiled its new Roadster model on Thursday evening in a live demonstration that showed off the vehicle’s capability for limited flight using pressurized air.
CEO Elon Musk said production of the long-awaited vehicle was set to begin in 2028, “actually.”
Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) shares rose over 3% in aftermarket trade following the reveal. They had fallen more than 1% earlier.
Tesla debuted the model in a live event at SpaceX’s McGregor, Texas test facility. The vehicle was able to climb a curved ramp at a controlled pace, and jumped the ramp at a full inversion before using its air thrusters to correct its orientation and land on all four wheels.
Tesla also demonstrated the Roadster’s ability of short flight, having the car jump and hover over a set of parked cars and a semitruck. Tesla is calling the feature short-burst flight.
Get more breaking news on Tesla and Musk by subscribing to InvestingPro
The Roadster uses air-based rocket boosters, a non-combustion-based system that involves using cold, compressed gas to generate thrust. SpaceX uses the same technology in some of its rocket ships.
The car is able to generate suction to improve handling, and is also capable of driving on vertical surfaces. The Roadster demonstrated acceleration of 0-60 miles per hour in 0.81 seconds, using a combination of its compressed air and electric motor.
“We anticipate being able to do better than that,” Musk said, stating that the Roadster would be capable of a top speed of Mach 0.5, or half the speed of sound.
Musk said the Roadster was "not necessarily a safety optimized car," but that it would be an "actual car that’s on roads."
The car carries about 260 kilograms of air, and is capable of recharging its air tank using an onboard compressor that operates autonomously.
Musk touted the vehicle as a product of collaboration between Tesla and SpaceX. The Roadster was operated remotely for the demonstration.
Tesla had first teased a second-generation Roadster in November 2017, but had then repeatedly delayed unveiling the vehicle until October 2026.
The Roadster was back then touted as having a 0-60mph time of 1.9 seconds and a $200,000 base price.
The Roadster will likely compete with ultra-luxury EV offerings such as Ferrari’s Luce and upcoming models from Jaguar and Rolls Royce.
The new Roadster reveal comes as Tesla seeks to shore up its laggard automaking business, which has been struggling with a sales decline for two years. A mix of heightened competition in China, plus controversy around Musk’s political leanings, had battered Tesla sales since 2024.
Musk had earlier touted artificial intelligence and robotics as the next big growth levers for Tesla. The automaker even discontinued production of its X and S models to convert their manufacturing lines into producing its Optimus robot.

title: Mideast war alters global bunker buying patterns, industry execs say
full_text:
Nasdaq ends higher in big rebound as bond rally offsets tech softness, hot PPI
By Jeslyn Lerh
SINGAPORE, Oct 16 (Reuters) - The US-Israeli war on Iran has altered bunker buying patterns for shippers globally as they turned to more spot and shorter-term purchases to cope with volatile prices while exploring more alternative locations for supply security, industry executives said.
More than seven months since the start of the conflict with Iran, prices of marine fuels remained well over 70% versus pre-war levels, according to data from bunker traders.
Rerouting and diversions of vessels due to blockades at key waterways in the Middle East have also driven shippers to diversify refuelling locations, making them less inclined to lock in a longer-term contracts at one particular port, the executives said.
"The frequency of stems (spot purchases) is getting higher because a lot of owners will bunker the minimum to reach the next port if the market shoots up," said Peter Grunwaldt, chief executive officer at Seascale Energy and head of bunkering at tanker company Hafnia, on the sidelines of the Singapore International Bunkering conference.
Spot purchases give more flexibility to the shipowner, who decides whether to buy bunkers in that instance, depending on the daily price, suppliers said. In contrast, if they lock into a longer term contract, they will have to lift the agreed volume regardless of how the price swings.
"When prices are elevated, you have this notion that if prices fall tomorrow, you don’t want to be too exposed," said Mikkel Kannegaard, chief operating officer at Bunker Holding, the world’s largest bunker seller by volume.
"So we have seen a trend where longer-term contracts have become less common," he told Reuters, adding that bunker trade has become more complex amid a more fragmented market.
Choong Zhen Mao, executive director at Singapore-based Equatorial Marine Fuel, said the duration of term contracts with buyers had shortened to a quarter or even a month, versus longer terms like six months or one year, before the war.
ALTERNATIVE BUNKER PORTS
Besides breaking up the size of bunker purchases, shippers are also turning to alternative locations to seek bunker supplies and refuel as hostilities around the United Arab Emirates’ Fujairah port, which used to be a top supplier, intensified, the executives said.
"Around the Arabian Gulf in particular, traditional bunkering patterns are being torn apart," said Seascale’s Grunwaldt.
"Diversions from Fujairah have clearly driven more enquiries to surrounding ports, so we now bunker in more ports than we used to," he added.
"Ports that were only used sporadically before, such as Port Louis, Colombo and Salalah, are now being used more frequently," he said, referring to ports in Mauritius, Sri Lanka and Oman.
Bunker Holding’s Kannegaard said he had seen more demand emerging in Africa and South Asia.
In response to the Middle East disruption, Vitol began bunkering at the Gwadar Port in Pakistan in July, offering a location outside the Strait of Hormuz from which to serve customers operating in the Gulf region.
"Diversification is essential, both to manage today’s disruptions and to build longer-term resilience," Vitol’s Head of Asia Kieran Gallagher said.
"In the near term, that means broadening geographic sources of supply and developing new trade routes for conventional fuels."

TOKYO, Oct 16 (Reuters) - Japan’s core consumer inflation in September likely exceeded the central bank’s 2% target as higher energy prices driven by the Middle East conflict fed through to households, a Reuters poll showed on Friday.
• The nationwide core consumer price index (CPI), which includes energy items but excludes fresh food prices, is expected to have risen 2.1% in September from a year earlier, according to a poll of 15 economists

• "Amid the emerging deterioration of the situation in Iran, growth is expected to accelerate for food items excluding rice as well as daily necessities," said Ryosuke Katagi, a market economist at Mizuho Securities

title: World Bank’s Banga sets goal of quintupling critical minerals financing in five years
full_text:

BANGKOK, Oct 16 (Reuters) - World Bank President Ajay Banga on Friday said the development lender has set a goal of quintupling its critical minerals business in five years, and has identified 20 countries that it can partner with on critical minerals development projects.
Banga revealed the new goal in prepared remarks to a plenary session at the International Monetary Fund and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok.
"In critical minerals, we plan to quintuple our business in five years," Banga said. "This week, we launched our first country compacts with MDB partners—to build local industries and keep more jobs and value at home."
The World Bank’s new Metals and Minerals implementation plan is targeting $19 billion in critical minerals financing over the fiscal 2026-2030 period, compared with $3.6 billion in the fiscal 2021-2025 period.
Critical minerals development is an area where the United States, the World Bank’s largest shareholder, has called for the bank to devote more financing resources.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said earlier this week that he wanted the bank to play a bigger role in enabling critical minerals mining and processing capacity through project de-risking and finance and investment in enabling infrastructure. He said this includes deep-sea mining projects.
Banga did not mention deep-sea mining, but the bank’s metals plan calls for a "precautionary approach" to the nascent sector, adding that any engagement and investments must be consistent with applicable bank policies.
Banga reviewed the World Bank’s overall increases in financing during the 2026 fiscal year that ended on June 30, including mobilizing $112 billion in private capital, a more than threefold increase from the 2022 fiscal year, before he assumed his role.
Alongside lending from the World Bank’s own balance sheet, this brought the group’s total financing to $230 billion for fiscal 2026, he said.

As he has largely done since taking over at the helm of the Fed earlier this year, Warsh did not reveal any specific insight into the central bank's rate trajectory. Instead, he stressed that he doesn't "believe in saying now what I might do at the meetings that we have in the balance of this year."
Despite Warsh's resistance to forward guidance, some of his Fed colleagues have suggested in recent weeks that while further rate hikes may be needed to corral inflation, they are awaiting more data. In September, the Fed lifted borrowing costs by 25 basis points, highlighting a desire to cool price growth back to its 2% level.

title: Fed’s Warsh says AI boom could boost growth, but warns of bumpy transition
full_text:

Investing.com-- Artificial intelligence could deliver a significant boost to economic productivity over the medium term, though the transition is likely to be bumpy and poses challenges for monetary policymakers, Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said on Friday, reiterating the central bank's commitment to price stability.
Speaking at an International Monetary Fund forum during the annual meetings in Bangkok, Warsh said AI was initially boosting demand before its longer-term benefits flowed through to the supply side of the economy.
"I do fundamentally believe" AI would deliver a positive supply shock in the medium term, Warsh said, describing the technology as one of the most consequential changes to the U.S. and global economy in his lifetime.
However, the transition would bring uncertainty over employment, market structure and which companies would ultimately benefit, he said, adding that policymakers needed to assess the technology's implications for inflation, productivity and financial stability.
Warsh said the Fed remained committed to restoring price stability after removing some monetary policy accommodation at its September meeting, but declined to signal its next move.
"I don't prejudge meetings," he said, adding that policymakers would assess developments in output, employment and inflation ahead of their remaining meetings this year.
He also highlighted persistent inflation as a common challenge for central banks worldwide, noting that policymakers had demonstrated resolve in pursuing price stability despite differing economic conditions.
Warsh said the U.S. economy was benefiting from a substantial investment surge that extended beyond AI, providing tailwinds for growth. The global economy had also proved more resilient than he might have expected several months earlier despite geopolitical tensions and conflicts.
The Fed is examining AI's implications through external task forces, including one on productivity and jobs, which is scheduled to hold its first field hearing in the San Francisco Bay Area on November 16.
Warsh said policymakers needed to question established assumptions and remain open to new ideas as technological and structural changes reshape the economy.

title: Ofwat proposes £280,000 package after Hafren Dyfrdwy sewage breaches

Investing.com -- Britain’s water regulator Ofwat said on Friday it had found Welsh water company Hafren Dyfrdwy in breach of its legal obligations over its wastewater treatment works and network, and proposed a £280,000 enforcement package, subject to a public consultation.
Ofwat said the company failed to effectively provide drainage and deal with the contents of its sewers, and had historically breached licence requirements to have adequate processes and systems in place.
The package is larger than the £255,000 penalty Ofwat said it would otherwise have imposed, equal to 3.5% of the company’s annual turnover.
A penalty would have gone to the Consolidated Fund operated by HM Treasury.
Instead, the money stays in the water sector and will be spent on improving service for customers and the local environment.
The company and its shareholders will pay, not customers through higher bills. The work must be delivered by 2030.
It includes two storm water balancing tanks at the Llansantffraid Sewage Pumping Station to reduce spills, and work with the Llanfyllin Dolydd Building Preservation Trust to support a wetland habitat at the Llanfyllin Workhouse, expected to be completed by 2030.
Ofwat said the company now has the right processes in place but must rectify all outstanding issues and ensure future compliance.
“Our investigation found unacceptable breaches by Hafren Dyfrdwy, which have resulted in excessive spills from storm overflows,” said Lynn Parker, Ofwat’s senior director for enforcement.
The case is the ninth in Ofwat’s wider wastewater investigation, which has secured more than £300 million in enforcement packages and fines.

title: Besi shares slide on report of ASML developing competing hybrid bonding product
full_text:

Investing.com -- Shares in Dutch chip equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries (Besi) fell nearly 3% on Friday after research firm SemiAnalysis said ASML is developing a rival tool for hybrid bonding, the advanced chip-stacking process that is Besi’s main growth driver.
Besi was down 2.66% at €159.05, while ASML Holding rose 1.11% to €1,480.40, as of 08:02 ET (12:02 GMT).
The report said ASML filed 27 bonding patent families between December 2022 and November 2024, most for die-to-wafer bonding, and the true count is likely higher because later filings are not yet public.
Besi has led die-to-wafer bonding and is the only supplier with tools in volume production, SemiAnalysis said. Everyone else is still trying to get a first tool qualified.
SemiAnalysis expects advanced logic to adopt ASML’s tool first, calling that “bad news for Besi.”
Logic accounts for most of Besi’s hybrid bonding business, concentrated at TSMC and Intel, both of which ASML has worked with for more than two decades.
Besi’s HBM prospects are also weakening, SemiAnalysis said, as Korean challengers catch up and HBM adoption of die-to-wafer bonding is expected to slip to 2029 or beyond.
ASML’s design differs from conventional machines, where a bond head picks each die off a diced wafer and places it.
Instead, each die moves on its own holder around a track past inspection, cleaning, plasma activation and measurement stations before reaching a bonding station, where a chuck lifts the bottom wafer to meet it.
SemiAnalysis said ASML could gain an edge in alignment accuracy and particle control, the two factors that set bonding yield, but still needs to solve challenges around feed-forward metrology, die-to-wafer contact, modifying non-bonding tools and keeping the loop clean. It expects ASML to price its tools at a premium to peers.
The Elec reported in March that ASML had started architecture design of a hybrid bonder with Prodrive Technologies and VDL ETG.
Die-to-wafer hybrid bonding has moved slowly because the industry lacks mature tools combining alignment accuracy and throughput, SemiAnalysis said, keeping cost per die high. It runs in volume only in logic, where AMD has shipped hybrid-bonded V-Cache since 2022.

A problem with the anti-ice system on 737 MAX engines that arose in 2023 further delayed certification of the MAX 7 and 10.
The delays have helped European rival Airbus’ A321neo secure a greater share of the large single-aisle market. Boeing has said the MAX 10 will be a major cash-flow driver in its ongoing financial recovery following years of crises and controversies.
Airlines have ordered nearly 1,500 MAX 10s, and the model accounts for about 30% of Boeing’s outstanding 737 backlog. The planemaker has already built a handful of MAX 10s awaiting delivery.
The bigger plane that can carry more passengers is crucial to several airlines’ growth plans. Major customers for the MAX 10 include United Airlines, Alaska, Ryanair, Delta Air Lines and American Airlines.
A glitch with the latest update of the 737 MAX’s navigation software threatened to further delay certification when Boeing disclosed it in late September. However, the FAA determined on October 2 that it did not pose a safety concern and did not require Boeing to fix the problem as a condition of certifying the plane.
Boeing is still working on certifying the 777-9, its largest jetliner in production, which is already six years behind schedule. The company has said it expects to complete certification and begin deliveries in 2027.

WASHINGTON, Oct 16 (Reuters) - White House press secretary Katie Zacharia was fired after less than a week on the job, two US officials said on Friday, after a rocky start as President Donald Trump’s top spokesperson.
Zacharia was "let go" and is "transitioning out" of the press secretary position, according to two separate White House officials. She faced days of questions about her legal credentials and criticism of her performance in a news briefing and interviews.
The departure leaves Trump without a key public messenger just over two weeks before November’s midterm elections, a critical period when the president is seeking to tout his administration’s accomplishments and help his fellow Republicans retain control of Congress.
Trump told reporters earlier on Friday that he had asked Zacharia to reconsider whether to continue in her role after facing tough press coverage during her first days on the job.
"I told her: ’I think you’re better off being happy, and I’m not sure you can ever be happy in this stuff.’ There’s nothing easy about this stuff," Trump told reporters as he departed the White House for a weekend trip.
He added: "I said to her honestly, ’If I were you, I’d reconsider... think about it. But I would reconsider.’" Trump said he intended to revisit the conversation with Zacharia later.
Zacharia started on Monday and held her debut White House briefing on Tuesday. She said she received a call about the press secretary role on October 7 and was offered the job to succeed Karoline Leavitt a week ago.
She soon faced questions about her career, which she said included a tenure practicing law. Trump had also described her as an attorney.
"I practiced international transaction law, with all the appropriate credentials," Zacharia said in an emailed statement on Wednesday.
Reuters could not find records showing the Pepperdine University law school graduate was registered as an attorney or member of the bar in any US state or the District of Columbia.
During a Fox News interview on Thursday, Zacharia said she did not pass the bar exam. Law school graduates cannot legally practice law in the US without first being admitted to a state bar.
Zacharia and the White House did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment about her firing.
Earlier on Friday, she told reporters at the White House that she was looking forward to working with the press.
Trump hired Zacharia after expressing concerns about the media coverage of his administration, feeling he needed a new spokesperson who could amplify his achievements, according to two people familiar with the conversations.
In a phone interview with Fox on Friday, Trump said he was in no rush to name a new press secretary.
Zacharia’s quick exit meant she had what is believed to be the shortest tenure of any press secretary in the role’s history.
"Records are made to be broken," Anthony Scaramucci, who served as director of communications for 10 days during Trump’s first administration, said on X. "But I take no pleasure in other people’s pain."

full_text:

By Summer Zhen and Anirban Sen
TOKYO/NEW YORK, Oct 16 (Reuters) - Global hedge funds suffered steep losses this week, battered by a sharp unwind of a swathe of AI bets, with Asia-focused funds hit the hardest.
Investors are increasingly questioning whether massive AI spending can pay off anytime soon as elevated inflation keeps borrowing costs high. Wall Street ended the week sharply lower on Friday, with AI-related technology stocks including CoreWeave and Broadcom under renewed pressure, while a jump in oil prices spooked traders heading into the weekend.
CoreWeave has been one of the biggest casualties of the latest selloff, with the data center operator’s bonds selling off sharply this week, pushing yields above 15%.
Global fundamental long-short funds, or stock pickers, lost money every single day this week, the Goldman Sachs prime brokerage unit said in a note to clients, with losses for the week to October 15 coming to 2.9%. For the year to date, they have gains of 14.3%.
"Following a sharp AI unwind on Wednesday and week-over-week, global equities were net sold again yesterday (Thursday) though at a much slower pace, driven by continued risk unwinds with long sales outpacing short covers," Goldman said in the note on Friday. "In dollar terms, yesterday’s global de-grossing activity — long selling and short covering combined — was roughly half of what we saw on Wednesday."
Goldman added that global AI stocks collectively have been sold by long-short fund managers for six straight sessions.
On Thursday, hedge funds across strategies retreated sharply, with stock pickers globally losing 0.9%. Among them, Asia-focused managers were down 2.6%, while tech-focused funds were off 2.0%. Global systematic long-short managers and multi-strategy funds also declined roughly 1%.
"What we saw was less a fundamental rejection of AI and more a classic, high-velocity unwind of a crowded trade meeting a macro reality check," said Bruno Schneller, managing partner at Erlen Capital Management, which invests in hedge funds. "Hotter-than-expected US inflation data forced markets to reassess the path of interest rates, putting immediate pressure on the most capital-intensive parts of the AI complex."
US inflation data this week increased expectations of further rate hikes, fueling declines in semiconductor and AI supply chain stocks.
Semiconductor-heavy markets bore the brunt of the selloff. South Korea’s benchmark KOSPI tumbled 8% to close at a six-month low on Thursday, while Taiwan stocks also lost more than 3%.
"From COVID through end-2025, all three broad strategies never fell more than 80 bps on the same day," Goldman Sachs said in an earlier note from Thursday, referring to fundamental equity long-short, systematic and multi-strategy trades.
The note added that this has now occurred three times this year: on February 4, July 28 and October 15.
Asia-focused stock pickers have lost 6.8% for the first half of this month and have erased more than half of the gains from their late-June peak, when they were up more than 40% for the year, according to Goldman Sachs.
"The interesting thing about this selloff is that it exposes just how much of the hedge fund industry has effectively been trading the same underlying theme, even when portfolios look very different on paper," said Schneller.
